owner.title: Owners and admins
owner.intro: Ten steps from a new account to a smooth daily routine. Tick each one off as you go; this page remembers.

steps.title: Request your store's account
steps.text: Fill in Create your store with your store's name, the Store ID your team will type, your POS and your time zone. A person at KloudC reviews it.

steps.title: Sign in for the first time
steps.text: Once approved, sign in with your Store ID, your username and the password you chose. If KloudC set the store up for you, use the one-time set-up link to choose your password.

steps.title: Connect your POS
steps.text: On Setup › Integrations, add your {pos} details, Save, then Test connection. Sales start syncing that night.

steps.title: Load your first inventory
steps.text: Upload {pos}'s retail items export on Home, exactly as {pos} gives it. Or, later, turn on Inventory from {pos}.

steps.title: Set vendor schedules
steps.text: On the Vendor Calendar, add each vendor's delivery days and order deadline. Suggested schedules can fill most of them in one go.

steps.title: Set up PO sections and vendor contacts
steps.text: Check how items group on your POs, and save each vendor's email so Send PO can reach them.

steps.title: Add your team
steps.text: On Users, add a login for each person and tick the pages they may open. Use Hide sales numbers for anyone who shouldn't see dollar amounts.

steps.title: Teams, checklists and News
steps.text: Create teams, build your daily checklists in the Checklist builder, and post a welcome on News.

steps.title: Install the app and choose alerts
steps.text: Install KloudC RetailOps on your phone, sign in, and pick your alerts under More › Notifications. Connect WhatsApp and email on Integrations too.

steps.title: Your daily routine
steps.text: Each morning: check Home and the Today card, build orders with Reorder Candidates or New order, send the PO, and confirm deliveries in Delivery Review.

staff.title: Staff
staff.intro: Seven steps to find your way around. You only see the pages your admin gave you, so skip any you don't have.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.text: Use your store's Store ID, the username your admin gave you, and your password. Change the password to your own on Change password.

steps.title: Home and the Today card
steps.text: Home shows what needs doing today. Each tile opens the page behind it.

steps.title: Fill in your daily checklist
steps.text: Open Daily Checklists, answer each question and Submit. A summary goes to your team's WhatsApp group.

steps.title: Upload an invoice
steps.text: When a delivery comes, upload the invoice on Invoices: pick the vendor, take a photo, Submit.

steps.title: Fix issues assigned to you
steps.text: On Fix Issues, close the items you have dealt with, with the reason that fits.

steps.title: Tasks, chat and News
steps.text: Check Team for your tasks, chat with your team, and confirm you've read any News that asks.

steps.title: Scan and print a label
steps.text: In the app, the Scan tab looks an item up by its barcode and prints its price label.

master.title: KloudC master
master.intro: Seven steps for running the platform: requests, stores, hosting, the audit log and support.

steps.title: Sign in with two-step
steps.text: Use Store ID PLATFORM, your username and password, then the 6-digit code. Set up two-step first if you haven't.

steps.title: Review requests
steps.text: On Requests, check each new store and approve it with a starter pack, or reject it with a friendly note.

steps.title: Watch provisioning
steps.text: On Stores, a new store moves from Setting up to Active. Retry set-up if it fails.

steps.title: Store status
steps.text: Suspend a store to pause it, Resume to turn it back on, and Archive to off-board it.

steps.title: Hosting requests
steps.text: Approve or reject moves to a dedicated server, and roll back within 7 days if needed.

steps.title: The audit log
steps.text: Every sign-in and change is listed on Audit. Check it before asking anyone what happened.

steps.title: Helping a store
steps.text: Answer support emails with the right guide, look only at what the case needs, and never ask for a password.
